gold_diagnosis: congenital unilateral hypoplasia of depressor anguli oris

1: The patient's symptoms of facial asymmetry and deviation of the right lower lip when smiling or crying, with otherwise normal facial movement and development, suggest a congenital condition affecting the facial muscles or nerves, and the absence of other significant findings supports this diagnosis.

The patient's presentation of isolated right lower lip deviation with otherwise symmetric facial movements and normal developmental milestones could also suggest congenital facial paresis, although the specific involvement of the lower lip points more strongly towards congenital unilateral lower lip palsy.
